findings.rationale: Claim (issue_present): invariant_name joins sanitized parts with the literal separator 'QqDbSepqQ', but safe() preserves alphanumerics, so user content can contain the separator and distinct part sequences collide: invariant_name(['db_not_null_after_backfill','t','cQqDbSepqQd']) equals invariant_name(['db_not_null_after_backfill','tQqDbSepqQc','d']). Two distinct (table, column) pairs then produce identical invariant names: the second registry.bind overwrites the first origin and two invariants with the same name are emitted. Evidence status: unverified — the join collision is directly computable from invariant_name; would need a reproduction test with such names, plus the presentation-time name splitting (outside the reviewed context), to confirm user-visible impact.

Claim (issue_present): lower_compose can panic on a syntactically valid compose document instead of returning the CoreError its doc comment promises for 'unknown aliases'. In the Common(Init) arm, rewrite_compose_statements collects resolve_alias_statement results and discards any error via .expect("compose alias validation occurs during lowering"); resolve_alias_qualified_name returns Err when a binder's qualified type name names a namespace that is not a declared alias, so e.g. `common init { forall x: missing.T { ... } }` panics. Sibling paths propagate the same error correctly with `?` (Common invariant/trans/reachable via rewrite_compose_item, sync params via resolve_alias_param). Evidence status: unverified — static reading of compose.rs only; would need a reproduction test running fsl-parse-kernel on such a document to observe the panic (exit 101) vs the documented exit-2 diagnostic.

Claim (issue_present): column_member is not injective. safe() preserves underscores, so distinct (table, column) pairs map to the same enum member: ('a','b_c') and ('a_b','c') both yield 'col_a_b_c'. Consequences inside lower_db_surface: the generated Column enum lists duplicate members; the init loop assigns column_exists/column_backfilled/column_not_null for both columns to the same map key, so one column's flags silently overwrite the other's (BTreeMap order decides); migrations and per-column not_null invariants referencing either column then operate on the merged key. The same non-injective safe() also collides migration action names ('migrate_add/x' vs 'migrate_add_x'). Evidence status: unverified — the name collision is directly computable from safe/column_member in db.rs; would need a reproduction test lowering such a dbsystem to confirm how the kernel treats duplicate enum members.

Claim (issue_present): fsl-parse-kernel reads the root file with fs::read_to_string(path).expect("read FSL source file"), so a missing or unreadable root path panics (Rust panic, exit 101) instead of using the binary's own error channel — eprintln + exit(2) — which it applies to parse errors from parse_kernel_source. The same missing-file condition for a compose dependency returns a clean CoreError via FsResolver::read, so the two entry paths behave inconsistently. Evidence status: unverified — static reading only; would need to run the binary on a missing path to observe the panic.
